Noise and double-texting, unchanged and still how this fails.

Never let anything compute a price. Three numbers on one proposal all look correct and only invoice.total is what the customer was quoted; the discount label itself is off by three points on at least one live proposal. Any change that sums, subtracts or applies a percentage reintroduces an $825 error. Read what the customer typed, not what is in the thread. Our own marketing arrives labelled inbound and byte-identical to what we sent. iPhone tapbacks arrive as inbound and are our own words quoted back. Inbound email arrives with no body at all. A similarity score cannot gate a draft. 'Customer wants to rent a car' — never offered, never answered — scores 75% on the reranker, one point below a genuine reschedule. Whether the retrieved exemplar is the same KIND of message is checkable; how similar it is, is not.

Instagram closes after 7 days, and a draft approved after the window shuts is rejected outright. This has already happened once, approved nine hours late.

On Discord specifically: server permissions are not enough, a channel-level override kept every channel unreadable until the bot was added to the channel's own permission list, and the failure is a silent 403 with no error anywhere.

sessions.title: Built a scoreboard that tests each Claude model 10 times per task: Sonnet 5.5 matched Opus 5.5 on all 50 runs at less than half the cost
shipped: Built a test bench that scores Claude models on 5 fixed tasks from our own work: a client text under Noah's product rules, pulling 12 fields out of a messy lead note, a phone-number cleaner checked against 14 hidden cases, drop-off days around the Tuesday to Thursday closure, and a 100 to 130 word explanation under a list of writing rules. Each task runs 10 times per model, because the same prompt gives different answers from run to run, and a script grades every answer, so no AI judge can tilt the score.

Ran the first full baseline on 10/18 (150 runs in about 5 minutes, $0.89 of usage): Opus 5.5 passed 50 of 50, Sonnet 5.5 passed 50 of 50, and Haiku 5.5 passed 46 of 50, with all 4 misses running past the word limit. Per run, Opus cost about 1.2 cents, Sonnet about half a cent, and Haiku 0.03 cents.
All 30 client texts across the three models kept Noah's product rules: no 'chip-proof', no 'hydrophobic', no stacked years called a warranty, no PeelClear, and no prices.

When the next model comes out, one command runs it through the same 5 tasks and shows whether it beats, ties, or trails the models in use, with a check that separates a real change from normal run-to-run wobble.
fixed: Caught that test runs started from the Claude desktop app inherit about 30 hidden app settings, which added about 300 tokens to every model's instructions and forced maximum effort. The bench now strips them, so a test started from the app scores the same as one started from Terminal. Any other script that runs Claude from the app has the same leak.

Found and fixed two bench bugs before they cost anything: one crashed run could have thrown away a whole batch's paid results, and a test edited mid-batch would have been stamped with the wrong version. Both are covered now, among 93 self-checks that run for free.
inProgress: Opus and Sonnet both scored 50 of 50, so these 5 tasks can catch a model getting worse but can't yet say which of the two is better. A harder second version of the tasks would answer that.
sessions.notes: This grades the models, not the business.
